Based on the retrieved healthcare Q&A matches, here's a clear and concise synthesis of answers to your user question:

Laparoscopic antireflux surgery significantly improves quality of life in patients whose symptoms are well-controlled with medical therapy. This means that if you have gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and your symptoms are managed effectively with medication, surgery may be an option to consider.

This approach is recommended because, although a noncomparative trial with a relatively short follow-up period was conducted, it suggests that patients who undergo laparoscopic antireflux surgery tend to experience significant improvements in their quality of life. However, it's essential to note that the benefits of surgery should not be overlooked and may vary from one patient to another.

It's also worth mentioning that other treatments, such as medical therapy with or without medication, can provide relief for many patients. The decision to pursue surgical intervention should be made in consultation with a healthcare professional who can assess your individual situation and help you weigh the potential benefits against any risks or complications.

In summary, if you have well-controlled GERD symptoms managed by medical therapy, laparoscopic antireflux surgery may offer significant improvements in quality of life.
